sentences.text:
This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act (M.V. Act) has been filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated January 20, 2019, passed by the Senior Civil NC:
2024:KHC:20234 Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Arkalgud, in MVC No.1697/2016.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Arkalgud
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimant filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, stating that on September 19, 2015, while he was traveling to Tumakuru on his motorcycle, the rider of another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-06/EM-7512 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and collided with his motorcycle.
Consequently, the claimant fell, and at that moment, the driver of a Honda City car, also driving in a rash and negligent manner, collided with the rider of the offending motorcycle.
3. The Tribunal, after evaluating the evidence on record, attributed contributory negligence to both the rider of the offending motorcycle and the driver of the car.
It awarded a total compensation of Rs.58,400/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petition until the date of realization.
Aggrieved by this decision, the claimant has filed an appeal seeking an enhancement of the compensation.

4. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, it is noted that the claimant was working as a manager and produced Exhibit P.27 to substantiate that he was earning a salary of Rs.47,000/- per month.
Considering the accident occurred in 2015, it is inferred that the claimant's income at that time was approximately Rs.40,000/- per month.

The claimant was an inpatient for 7 days, and Exhibit P.3 (the wound certificate) NC: 2024:KHC:20234 indicated that he suffered a fracture of the left wrist due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
5. It is undisputed that the claimant continued to work as a manager even after sustaining the fracture.
Therefore, he is not entitled to compensation for the loss of future income.

However,
considering the nature of the injuries and the fact that he was an inpatient for 3 days, it is appropriate to award an enhanced compensation of Rs.41,600/- in addition to the Rs.58,400/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
6. Thus, the claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-.
The enhanced compensation amount of Rs.41,600/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petition until the date of actual realization.
To this extent, the impugned award stands modified.
The other portion of the impugned award, insofar as it relates to fastening liability on the 2nd and 4th respondents (the insurance company) to pay equally 50% of the compensation is confirmed.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of.
